db_row_notes: baked-cubano-chicken: 'Dill Pickles' arrived on a different serving basis (100 g = 100 g) than the row the DB holds, and the two AGREE once put on one basis - the mapper's row scaled onto the DB's 1 oz = 28 g reproduces the DB's own numbers within 5 kcal and 0.5 g. Nothing was written and the household row stands, which is the rule.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Cooked, seasoned, shredded pork shoulder, sold refrigerated in tubs (Del Real, Kirkland) or made from a pork butt. 945 g at batch scale, so a major component and not a garnish. The pre-resolve table reports the board carries NO commodity and NO capture match for it, and no vocabulary row shares a core word. It is not any existing pork id I can see evidence of: deli-ham, diced-ham and spiral-ham are cured ham at different price classes, and the run's own pork-loin protein is a different, much leaner cut sold raw. If the estate already prices this food under another spelling - pulled-pork, pork-carnitas, pork-shoulder or pork-butt - alias it rather than minting a duplicate; a pork-shoulder alias is the likeliest correct answer and I would accept it, since the cooked yield is about 65% of raw.

registrar_rulings.reason: The food is already priced: pork-shoulder ('Pork Shoulder / Butt') is live in the feed at $1.94/lb cheapest at Sam's Club, and the recipe board already prices ~12 carnitas/pulled-pork recipes (slow-cooker-pork-carnitas-bowl, pulled-pork-enchilada-bake, etc.) off this raw cut with the recipe doing the cooking. The dossier's sweep missed it only because 'carnitas' shares no token with 'pork' - the kielbasa seam. pork-shoulder's exclude list ('pulled', 'seasoned', 'smoked') shows prepared tubs (Del Real-style) were deliberately kept out of this row, so a new carnitas id would put the same pork shoulder on the board at raw and tub prices simultaneously. Follow-up: add carnitas -> pork-shoulder to recipe-floor-id-map.json (both lb, units match) via the sanctioned editor, and let the recipe spec carry the ~65% cooked-yield conversion, matching the estate's existing pulled-pork recipes.

macro_cross_check.verdict: Protein PASSES and matches the source to within 2% - so no portion is wrong. Calories exceed the 800 ceiling by 10-20% on either bean basis and this recipe is a live retirement risk at the band gate.
